messages:
olivia: quick sanity check — i'm starting a short admin entitlement tidy for infra accounts today, aiming to remove stale elevated grants and ensure KMS usage is tied to service owners. will coordinate with oncall. ETA: 48h. ping if you own any infra-* roles

devin: noted. can you post the list of accounts you're targeting? I have a couple that look like they need exceptions

olivia: pasted below — using `rbac-tool export --roles infra-admin,infra-deploy --age 90d` to generate

olivia: ```
# sample output
user: deploy-bot@example.com role: infra-deploy last_used: 2025-02-10
user: ci-runner@example.com role: infra-admin last_used: 2023-08-01
service: analytics-svc role: kms-encryptor last_used: 2026-01-12
```

samir: ci-runner should be rotated or downgraded. last_used 2023 => prob stale. +1 for removing infra-admin there

anya: quick KMS question — when you remove `kms-encryptor` bindings, do we need to rekey anything for analytics-svc? analytics team? @devin

devin: analytics team confirmed they call KMS only for envelope encryption; they have a fallback using service account creds. but we'll check audit logs first: run this CloudTrail filter

devin: ```aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --start-time 2025-01-01 --end-time 2026-03-01```

olivia: thanks. also checking Cloud Logging for `kms.decrypt` entries — sample query:

olivia: ```
resource.type="kms_key"
protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt"
jsonPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=~"analytics"
```

sec-bot: scheduled: admin-entitlement-check job started by olivia at 2026-03-20T10:15Z :gear:

oncall: FYI — if you prune infra-admin bindings during the day, tickets may blink for infra deploys. can we do canary first? a small subset of projects

olivia: yes — plan is canary 2 projects (infra-prod, infra-staging) + monitoring for 24h. rollback plan: reapply binding and force redeploy of failed jobs

samir: recommend adding an audit alert for `kms:Decrypt` by non-owner using existing alerting rule `sec-kms-unexpected` — better to catch regressions

anya: i've raised a quick doc in Confluence with owners list and rollback steps. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/ANON

devin: small nit — when you reapply bindings, use the `--grace-period 12h` flag on rbac-tool so CI jobs have a window to adapt

olivia: noted. action plan

olivia: - export current bindings (rbac-tool)
- run canary prune on infra-staging
- monitor logs/alerts 24h
- full prune if stable

olivia: tagging owners: @devin @samir @anya :white_check_mark:

oncall: i'll be on rotation today, will respond to alerts. threw a calendar block at 11:30 for rollback window

devin: doing a final pass on svcacct keys, will drop keys > 180d unused. sharing list in #help later

samir: if you want automation, I have a tiny script that correlates rbac export + cloudtrail and emits CSV. happy to share

olivia: please share. also, if anyone sees anything immediate (failed deploys, elevated access errors) ping here and DM oncall
